title: Nobody's Answering
briefing: The checkout page times out whenever it asks for a payment. The payments pods look perfectly healthy, and the Service in front of them exists, yet nobody answers. A toolbox pod is available to try the Service from the inside: `kubectl exec toolbox -- curl http://payment`. Find out why the call goes nowhere and make it answer, without touching the payments pods.
objective: Make http://payment answer from inside the cluster.
hints: Try the call yourself from the toolbox and read curl's error. 'Connection refused' on a Service usually means that nothing stands behind it.
A Service sends traffic to the pods its selector matches. Compare what the Service selects with the labels the pods really carry.
`kubectl describe service payment` shows the selector and the endpoints it found; `kubectl get pods --show-labels` shows the labels.
Change the Service to select the pods' labels (`kubectl patch service payment -p ...`, or apply a corrected manifest). The pods themselves are not the problem.

assert.label: the payment Service has both payments pods behind it

constraints.label: the payments Deployment was left alone
the payment Service was not deleted

findings.clue: From inside the cluster the call is refused: the Service exists, but nothing answers behind it.
The Service has no endpoints at all: its selector, app=payment, matches no ready pod.
The pods are labelled app=payments, with an s, and tier=backend. The Service selects app=payment.
